name: Shemaiah the Nehelamite
charge: Sending letters from Babylon to have Jeremiah put in prison and in the stocks; prophesying a lie
summary: From the first captivity Shemaiah wrote to the priests in Jerusalem, naming Jeremiah a madman and asking why he had not been put in the stocks. Zephaniah the priest read the letter in Jeremiah's ears, and the answer came back to Babylon: Shemaiah would have no man to dwell among the people, and would not see the good the Lord would do.
offense: Shemaiah sent letters in his own name from Babylon, urging Zephaniah the priest to restrain Jeremiah as a madman who made himself a prophet. He objected to Jeremiah's instruction that the captivity would be long and that the exiles should build houses and plant gardens. The message he attacked was the Lord's direction for the captives. Shemaiah sought to use priestly authority and imprisonment to silence it. Zephaniah read the letter to Jeremiah, and the Lord exposed Shemaiah as a man He had not sent, who had caused the people to trust in a lie.
judgment: God declared punishment upon Shemaiah and his seed. He would have no man dwelling among this people and would not behold the good the Lord would do for them, because he had taught rebellion against the Lord. Shemaiah opposed the word governing the years of waiting and was denied a share in the promised good beyond them. His objection to a long captivity could not shorten the time God had appointed. The letter intended to procure Jeremiah's restraint instead became the occasion for a sentence against its author.

verses.text: Thus shalt thou also speak to Shemaiah the Nehelamite, saying,

Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, Because thou hast sent letters in thy name unto all the people that are at Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,

The Lord hath made thee priest in the stead of Jehoiada the priest, that ye should be officers in the house of the Lord, for every man that is mad, and maketh himself a prophet, that thou shouldest put him in prison, and in the stocks.
Now therefore why hast thou not reproved Jeremiah of Anathoth, which maketh himself a prophet to you?
For therefore he sent unto us in Babylon, saying, This captivity is long: build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them.
And Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the ears of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then came the word of the Lord unto Jeremiah, saying,

Send to all them of the captivity, saying, Thus saith the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite; Because that Shemaiah hath prophesied unto you, and I sent him not, and he caused you to trust in a lie:

Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite, and his seed: he shall not have a man to dwell among this people; neither shall he behold the good that I will do for my people, saith the Lord; because he hath taught rebellion against the Lord.
For thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Let not your prophets and your diviners, that be in the midst of you, deceive you, neither hearken to your dreams which ye cause to be dreamed.
For they prophesy falsely unto you in my name: I have not sent them, saith the Lord.
Now Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard that Jeremiah prophesied these things.
Then Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet, and put him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the Lord.

And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from the Lord your God, which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust thee out of the way which the Lord thy God commanded thee to walk in. So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee.

entries.commentary: Jeremiah sent a letter from Jerusalem to the residue of the elders, the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried captive to Babylon, after Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the princes, the carpenters, and the smiths had departed. Just like in this captivity, our people still carried those talents and skills; we had carpenters and we had blacksmiths.

The Most High tells the captives that even in their captivity they should build houses and dwell in them, buy homes, plant gardens and eat the fruit of them. They are to take wives and beget sons and daughters, take wives for their sons and husbands for their daughters, that they may be increased and not diminished, and seek the peace of the city where He caused them to be carried away, for in the peace thereof they shall have peace. -

Let not the false prophets and diviners in the midst of the people deceive them, nor their dreams; today Christianity has so-called prophets and Islam has so-called prophecy, but they deceive people because that is not the right way to serve the right God. After seventy years are accomplished at Babylon the Most High will visit them and perform His good word to return them, for His thoughts toward them are of peace and not of evil, to give them an expected end; the same is happening today, knowledge is being increased, we are finding out who we are and coming back to God's laws to be saved out of this captivity. When they call upon Him, seek Him, and search for Him with all their heart, He will be found of them and turn away their captivity, gathering them from all the nations and places whither He drove them; this is why the leadership goes out and teaches in the four corners of the earth, because all our people have been driven to the four corners.

Because they said the Lord had raised them up prophets in Babylon, the Most High declares He will send the sword, the famine, and the pestilence upon them and make them like vile figs that cannot be eaten, and deliver them to be a curse, an astonishment, a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations. This is because they had not hearkened to His words, which He sent by His servants the prophets, rising up early; so it behooves us to follow God's laws, for the prophets today are the ones going out teaching on the corners every Sabbath and seven days a week. The Most High never comes down here Himself to speak to the people; He speaks through His servants the prophets. -

Concerning Ahab the son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesied a lie in His name, the Most High would deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar to be slain before the captives' eyes. They would become a curse, the Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire, because they committed villainy in Israel, committed adultery with their brothers' wives, and spoke lying words in His name. -

To Shemaiah the Nehelamite: because he sent letters in his own name to all the people at Jerusalem and to Zephaniah the priest, claiming the Lord had made Zephaniah priest in the stead of Jehoiada to put every man that makes himself a prophet in prison and the stocks, and asking why he had not reproved Jeremiah for telling the captives their captivity was long and to build houses. Zephaniah read the letter in the ears of Jeremiah, and the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, for the Lord was dealing with Jeremiah, that was the difference. Because Shemaiah prophesied when the Lord sent him not and caused the people to trust in a lie, the Most High would punish him and his seed; he shall not have a man to dwell among the people nor behold the good the Lord will do, because he taught rebellion against the Lord.

Pashur the priest, chief governor in the house of the Most High, hears Jeremiah prophesy, smites him, and puts him in the stocks in the high gate of Benjamin. When he is let out the next day, Jeremiah tells him the Most High has renamed him Magor-missabib, a terror to himself and all his friends, for they shall fall by the sword of the king of Babylon. All Judah, all the strength and treasures of the city, and Pashur's whole household will be carried captive to Babylon, and Pashur will die there and be buried there with all the friends to whom he prophesied lies.

Jeremiah is going through it so bad, mocked and reproached daily, that he says he will not make mention of the Most High nor speak any more in His name. Just like us when we go out to camp, if somebody does not speak evil of us every time we do something big, there is a hater or somebody trying to demonize us. But the word was in his heart like a burning fire shut up in his bones; he was weary with holding it in and could not stay, he had to blast them, he could not hold it.

Jeremiah hears the defaming of many and his familiar friends watching for his stumbling, hoping to be enticed against him and take their revenge. The Most High is with him as a mighty terrible one, so his persecutors will stumble, not prevail, and be greatly ashamed in an everlasting confusion that will never be forgotten. He commits his cause to the Most High who tries the righteous and sees the reins and the heart, and sings praise because He delivers the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers.

Crushed by the persecution, Jeremiah curses the day he was born and the man who brought his father the news of a man child, wishing that man to be like the cities the Most High overthrew. He asks why he came forth out of the womb only to see labor and sorrow and to have his days consumed with shame.

The prophet or dreamer of dreams who speaks to turn you away from the Lord your God was put to death under the kingdom. Today Israel is in the land of its oppressors and cannot exact that judgment, and no kind of violence is advocated; the deceived and the deceiver are his, and the judgment belongs to the Most High. What is done today: mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned, and avoid them. The doctrine learned is the law, for I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law. Going contrary to the laws of marriage, of the sabbath, of raising children righteously, or of going to thy brother alone when there is an ought between you, and secretly enticing others to follow, is how one turns people away from the Lord; those men and those women have to be put out from among the body.

If thy brother, thy son, thy daughter, the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend which is as thine own soul entice thee secretly to serve other gods: these are the people closest to you, the ones that can have influence on you. Thou shalt not consent, nor hearken, nor pity, nor spare, neither shalt thou conceal him, meaning hide him; when wickedness is concealed, the whole nation is put in jeopardy. Trust in a person is no cover for your soul: when someone you love and trust has the devil on them, they will lead you astray. Nobody can make you do anything, but they can influence you; do not give anyone that credit and let them cause you to lose your crown. This is why [Leviticus 5:1](/bible/leviticus/5#v1) is opened at the start of class: if you know of anything, you are supposed to utter it. Many grew up on snitches get stitches, but in repentance we have to understand that concealing sin is part of why Israel is in the condition it is in, and we have to teach righteousness. It is that simple.

If certain men, the children of Belial, withdraw the inhabitants of a city, saying, let us go and serve other gods: inquire, make search, and ask diligently, and if it be truth and the thing certain, that city was smitten with the edge of the sword, gathered into the midst of the street, and burnt with fire, an heap for ever, not to be built again. Achan is the example of this kind of judgment: Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing, and one man's folly kindled the anger of the Lord against all Israel. Wars Israel had been winning without losing a man began to be lost, and Joshua had to search and seek out who had committed the crime in Israel. All Israel stoned Achan with stones and burned him with fire in the valley of Achor, and the Lord turned from the fierceness of his anger; righteous judgment lifted the wrath and the people were able to move forward.
